disease_education.body: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies are severe, mostly early-onset epilepsies in which both the underlying aetiology (often a single-gene variant) and the frequent epileptic activity itself impair development. The term was formalised in the ILAE 2017 classification, and the 2022 ILAE syndrome papers organise named syndromes (Dravet, LGS, infantile epileptic spasms syndrome, early-infantile DEE, etc.) by age at onset. Seizures are typically drug-resistant and accompanied by intellectual disability, motor, behavioural, sleep and feeding problems. In a New Zealand cohort the cumulative incidence of DEE was 169 per 100,000 children (about 1 in 590).
disease_education.verification: mixed: incidence search-verified; ILAE framing recalled

disease_education.body: SCN2A encodes Nav1.2, a voltage-gated sodium channel in excitatory neurons. Wolff et al. (Brain 2017; 71 new + 130 published patients) showed two broad groups: early-infantile onset (<3 months), associated with gain-of-function missense variants and good response to sodium channel blockers; and later onset (>=3 months), associated with loss-of-function (including all truncating variants), where sodium channel blockers were rarely effective and sometimes worsened seizures. The later-onset group includes West syndrome, myoclonic-atonic epilepsy, LGS-like and ESES-like phenotypes; loss-of-function variants also cause autism/intellectual disability without epilepsy. In one 72-patient cohort seizure onset ranged from day 1 of life to 2.5 years.

SCN8A encodes Nav1.6, concentrated at the axon initial segment and nodes of Ranvier. The 2024 global Delphi consensus defines five phenotypes ranging from severe DEE (onset ~0-6 months) and mild/moderate DEE (onset ~4-12 months) through self-limited (familial) infantile epilepsy to neurodevelopmental disorder with generalized epilepsy and NDD without epilepsy. Gain-of-function variants underlie the DEE and self-limited phenotypes; loss-of-function variants are associated with NDD with generalized epilepsy (absence) or without epilepsy.

disease_education.topic: Why sodium channel blockers help GoF and hurt LoF
disease_education.body: In gain-of-function disease the mutant channel passes too much current (slowed fast inactivation, faster recovery, larger persistent current), so drugs that block sodium channels (phenytoin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lacosamide, often at high doses) reduce the excess. In loss-of-function disease the channel is already under-active, so further block can aggravate seizures; the SCN8A consensus calls sodium channel blockers relatively contraindicated in LoF and levetiracetam relatively contraindicated in GoF. Functional class is usually inferred from age at onset and phenotype because functional assays are rarely available at the time of prescribing.

SCN8A-DEE caregivers report high seizure burden with multiple seizure types and multiple comorbidities; SCN2A early-onset DEE presents in the first days to weeks of life with tonic/focal seizures, sometimes evolving to epileptic spasms. Dravet typically starts with prolonged febrile hemiclonic or generalized seizures or status epilepticus in the first year, and LGS is defined by multiple seizure types including tonic and drop seizures. Seizure types counted in trials are 'countable motor seizures'.

Beyond seizures, DEEs carry intellectual disability, motor impairment/hypotonia, movement disorders, autism features, sleep and gastrointestinal problems. Treatment of SCN2A disorders remains primarily seizure control plus supportive therapies for autism and developmental delay, and the best treatment of SCN2A movement disorders is unknown. Praxis frames relutrigine OLE data as including developmental/'disease-modifying' potential, a claim not yet established by controlled data.

In a review of 190 published SCN8A patients overall mortality was 5.3% and 1.6% died of definite/probable SUDEP, while other reviews cite SUDEP in ~10% of SCN8A patients and note precise rates are unavailable. In a genetic-DEE cohort SCN2A accounted for 33% and SCN8A for 30% of deaths (shares of deaths, not rates). For Dravet, reported mortality ranges 3.7-20.8% across studies, with a Dravet-specific mortality rate of 15.84/1,000 person-years and SUDEP rate of 9.32/1,000 person-years in one cohort versus 4.4/1,000 person-years in a later population-based estimate.

A literature review of DEE caregiver impact found mean annual direct costs per patient of $24,048-$80,545 across studies, driven by home-based and inpatient care, with caregiver depression symptoms reported in up to 70.7%. A 2025 systematic review of indirect costs (Dravet, LGS, TSC) reports 35-45% of families had a caregiver leave employment, plus absenteeism and presenteeism. No US cost-of-illness study specific to SCN2A or SCN8A was found.

Most DEE patients survive into adulthood with persisting seizures and lifelong dependency; a 2025/26 Epilepsia Open review highlights gaps in evidence and care for adults with genetic DEEs. SCN8A stakeholders have published a research roadmap identifying natural-history data, biomarkers and trial-ready endpoints as priority gaps, supported by the International SCN8A Patient Registry.

patient_journey.description: SCN2A GoF: onset in first days-3 months; SCN8A severe DEE: 0-6 months; Dravet: prolonged febrile seizure in first year. Presentation is to ED, NICU or general paediatrician.
pain_points: seizures initially treated empirically (often levetiracetam or phenobarbital) before aetiology is known
levetiracetam is relatively contraindicated in SCN8A GoF per consensus

patient_journey.description: EEG, MRI, metabolic screen by child neurologist; drug resistance emerges quickly.
pain_points: multiple ASM trials before genetic result

patient_journey.description: NSGC 2022 guideline (AES-endorsed per secondary sources) strongly recommends genetic testing for all unexplained epilepsy at any age, with exome/genome or >25-gene panel first-tier, exome/genome conditionally preferred, then microarray. Rapid genome sequencing in infantile epilepsy (Gene-STEPS, n=100) gave a diagnosis in 43% with median 37 days from seizure onset to result; yield 74% with neonatal onset. Diagnoses changed treatment in 56%. Sponsored no-cost panels: Invitae/Labcorp 'Behind the Seizure' (US: child <10 with first unprovoked seizure at age 2-5; launched by BioMarin with Invitae, later multi-sponsor) and Invitae 'Unlock' (US: any child <18 with unprovoked seizure).
patient_journey.typical_duration: rapid genome ~5 weeks from onset in study setting; routine panels/exome weeks-months; historical odyssey length for SCN2A/SCN8A not found
pain_points: GoF vs LoF not reported on the lab result
eligibility windows of sponsored programs exclude many ages
sponsor list of Behind the Seizure not confirmed this session

patient_journey.description: Drug-resistant infants are referred to NAEC-accredited centers: 329 accredited at end of 2025 cycle (235 Level 4, 94 Level 3). Level 4 centers concentrate epilepsy genetics clinics, dietary therapy, VNS/surgery and trials.
pain_points: care remains split between local neurologist and tertiary center

patient_journey.description: Once SCN2A/SCN8A GoF is inferred (early onset + phenotype), sodium channel blockers become first line, often at supratherapeutic doses if tolerated; LoF patients are steered away from them.
pain_points: no FDA-approved therapy for SCN2A/SCN8A as of Nov 2026

patient_journey.description: Multiple ASMs, rescue medication, ketogenic diet, VNS; PT/OT/speech, feeding, sleep, orthopaedics, palliative care. Advocacy groups and registries become the main information source.
Families seek trials (EMBOLD/EMERALD, EMBRAVE, n-of-1 ASOs) via foundations' pipeline pages.
Adults with genetic DEEs face gaps in evidence and care; many adult neurologists lack DEE/genetics experience and adults may never have been sequenced.

pipeline.moa: Preferential persistent sodium-current inhibitor ('sodium-channel functional state modulator'); vendor data: IC50 141 nM persistent INa, ~60-fold vs peak
pipeline.key_data: EMBOLD cohort 1: 46% placebo-adjusted motor-seizure reduction over 16 wk (p=0.0354), >30% (n=5) seizure-free periods; registrational cohort 2 stopped early for efficacy: 53% placebo-adjusted reduction (p<0.0002). OLE: 86% reduction from baseline through 18 months (uncontrolled). BTD, orphan, eligible for PRV. Mid-cycle: no major issues, no AdCom; BIMO inspection done.
pipeline.next_catalyst: PDUFA 27 Dec 2026 (extended from 27 Sep 2026 after sensitivity analyses deemed major amendment); EMERALD topline Q4 2026 -> possible sNDA 2027
pipeline.status_note: Field team fully hired; top accounts and Tier 1/2 HCPs profiled

pipeline.key_data: EMBRAVE Part A (n=9, 3:1 vs sham, age 2-12): 77% placebo/sham-adjusted seizure reduction (p=0.015); 57% had >=28-day seizure-free period; 71% >=50% responders; no drug-related SAEs up to 8 mg. BTD granted.

unmet_needs.need: No FDA-approved therapy for SCN2A- or SCN8A-DEE
unmet_needs.detail: Relutrigine would be first if approved 27 Dec 2026; current care is off-label generic sodium channel blockers.

unmet_needs.need: Dose-limiting tolerability of non-selective sodium channel blockers
unmet_needs.detail: Consensus endorses supratherapeutic doses 'if tolerated'; preclinically PRAX-562 showed an improved protective index vs standard sodium channel blockers by preferentially inhibiting persistent current. Positioning: precision functional-state modulator that targets the hyperexcitable (disease-state) channel, enabling efficacy beyond what carbamazepine/phenytoin/lacosamide can deliver at tolerated doses, with RCT evidence (53% placebo-adjusted reduction on top of background therapy) and label. Risk: payers may require step-through generics.

unmet_needs.need: GoF vs LoF determination at point of care
unmet_needs.detail: Response to sodium channel blockade depends on variant function, but function is inferred from onset age; LoF patients may worsen. No clinical-stage option for SCN2A LoF.
Rapid genome gives answers in ~5 weeks and changes treatment in 56% of diagnosed infants, but is not universal; sponsored panels have narrow age windows.
Development, communication, sleep and movement disorder remain untreated; 'disease-modifying' claims (relutrigine, zorevunersen, ETX101) rest largely on open-label data.
SCN2A and SCN8A are over-represented among genetic-DEE deaths; rates are poorly quantified.
35-45% of families lose a caregiver's job; direct costs $24k-$80k/yr; no SCN2A/8A-specific US cost study.
Adults with genetic DEEs are under-diagnosed and under-served; transition pathways lacking.

EMBOLD is small with an unusual randomised-withdrawal-style placebo period; FDA extended review by 3 months after sensitivity analyses (major amendment). Mid-cycle found no major issues and no AdCom planned.

The sponsor cited ~5,000 US patients (SCN2A+SCN8A) in 2024 and 10K+ prevalent / ~5K diagnosed in November 2026; compare 1-3/100,000 for SCN2A alone and ~65 SCN8A births a year. Broad DEE: '>100k addressable' in 2024, over 200,000 in the August 2026 deck.

Neurocrine's Nav1.6-selective NBI-921352 was stopped for insufficient efficacy in SCN8A-DEE; Praxis's own vormatrigine missed POWER1 in focal epilepsy - mechanism selectivity alone does not guarantee efficacy.
CAP-002 patient death and trial closure; intrathecal ASO burden vs oral small molecule; elsunersen n=9.

unmet_needs.controversy: Broad-DEE basket labels vs gene-specific labels
unmet_needs.detail: Bexicaserin (DEEp OCEAN) and relutrigine (EMERALD) both pursue broad DEE; soticlestat's Phase 3 failures show risk in heterogeneous populations.

Epidiolex reached $1.06B in year 7 with no REMS and broad syndromes; Fintepla EUR 427M in year 5 despite echo REMS; Ztalmy ~$33M in year 3 in an ultra-orphan gene-defined population - the closest size analog to SCN2A/8A.
